key_insight: A foundation-model-based, data-efficient pipeline can detect rare duodenal epithelial neoplasia from whole-slide biopsy images with strong cross-site performance.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help pathology labs screen rare duodenal lesions more reliably when labelled training data are limited.
method: Five-hospital H&E WSI dataset of 8,027 normal and 401 neoplastic duodenal biopsies
Patch-level encoding with the Hibou-B foundation model plus PCA, Gaussian mixture modeling, and Random Forest classification
Compared global vs unsupervised site-specific standardisation and validated with leave-one-hospital-out and external testing
evidence_signal: The pipeline achieved 90% mean accuracy in leave-one-hospital-out cross-validation and 94% accuracy on an independent external hospital test set, with AUC up to 0.97.
watch_item: Performance was strong but the neoplastic class was still relatively small, so broader prospective validation is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: Data-efficient machine learning for the detection of duodenal neoplasia: a multi-centre study
